The reading
"No park geometry here. Just open ground, a treeline at the edge, and a sky that decides everything."

Wanstead Flats and the open ground toward Forest Gate carry a different register from a formal park. There's no Chahar Bagh here, no planted beds — just grass, wind, and a horizon that lets the sky do most of the talking. The trees stay at the edge, a line of structure against the openness rather than a canopy overhead.

The colour here isn't fixed the way a park's green is. Under clear sky, the grass turns golden, warmed by contrast with the blue above it. Under flat grey, that lift disappears and you see the ground's truer, quieter pigment. Both are honest. Neither is wrong. The field simply answers whatever sky it's given.

And that's only the daily shift. Across the year, this Locale changes more than any other — the field moving from green to gold to a weathered brown, the treeline at the edge bare through winter, full by late spring. Most views hold their character. This one keeps rewriting it. The wind rarely lets it settle either — the stillness here is punctuated, not silent.
